newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran says 1,000 more Kurdish refugees cross over.
newsitem.headline: Iran says 1,000 more Kurdish refugees cross over.

text.p: Iran said on Wednesday 1,000 more Kurdish refugees had crossed into its territory, joining tens of thousands who have fled northern Iraq since its takeover by a Baghdad-backed Kurdish faction in September.
The official Iranian news agency IRNA quoted a local Iranian official as saying the latest group of refugees crossed the border near the northwestern town of Baneh on Tuesday.
Laurens Jolles, an official of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), said there was a continued flow of refugees into Iran, although some were going back home.
"There are some people going back (to Iraq), but definitely not as many as the number of people who are arriving," Jolles told Reuters by telephone from Tehran.
He could not immediately confirm the numbers of refugees who had arrived on Tuesday.
"UNHCR is concerned about the situation of the refugees because of the proximity of the camps to the border and due to the climactic conditions," Jolles said.

Iran said in late September it was sheltering 65,000 refugees. Tehran has criticised international organisations, saying they were not providing enough help for the refugees living in tent camps in the cold mountainous border region.
UNHCR has urged Iran to move the camps away from the border.
